item.title: OnlyFans billionaire owner Leonid Radvinsky dies at 43 after cancer battle – Nehanda Radio
item.description: The billionaire owner of OnlyFans, Leonid Radvinsky, has died at the age of 43 following a prolonged battle with cancer.

item.title: Bobi Wine slams arrest of Tendai Biti as “cowardly attack” on democracy in Zimbabwe – Nehanda Radio
item.description: Ugandan opposition leader Robert Kyagulanyi Ssentamu, popularly known as Bobi Wine, has condemned the arrest of Zimbabwean politician Tendai Biti, describing it as a “cowardly attack” on citizens and democratic freedoms.

item.title: Temba Mliswa outburst displays selective memory and outrage on 2008 violence – Nehanda Radio
item.description: Outrage is seldom random in Zimbabwe’s political soap opera. It is cultivated, sharpened and unleashed with deliberate intent. The ongoing war of words between Temba Mliswa and retired Air Marshal Henry Muchena is not merely a clash of personalities.

item.title: The opposition in all but name: How Reform UK is governing by proxy on immigration – Nehanda Radio
item.description: The rise of Reform as a disruptive force in British politics was initially dismissed as peripheral agitation—loud, certainly, but electorally marginal. Yet such dismissals misunderstood the nature of political influence.

item.title: How can people who rejected a president in two elections now want him to extend his term? – Nehanda Radio
item.description: The political narrative currently being spun by loyalists of President Emmerson Mnangagwa is as audacious as it is intellectually dishonest.

item.title: Rejoice Ngwenya’s comparative lens on Zimbabwe’s constitutional amendments – Nehanda Radio
item.description: In his analysis of Constitutional Amendment Bill No. 3, Rejoice Ngwenya delivers a masterclass in exposing the hollow pretences of ZANU-PF’s constitutional engineering.

item.title: Air Marshal Henry Muchena is right to stand with Zimbabweans – Nehanda Radio
item.description: At a time when silence would be easier, Air Marshal (Retired) Henry Muchena has chosen principle over comfort and he is right to do so.

item.title: The gospel according to the herdsman: When the mooing stops, the clay cow is exposed – Nehanda Radio
item.description: Rutendo Benson Matinyarare, long celebrated as the chief acoustics engineer of Zimbabwe’s most delicate economic sculpture, the ZiG—now appears to have discovered an inconvenient truth: even the most beautifully crafted clay cow cannot moo indefinitely without cracking.

item.title: Who will drive the bus: Mamvura, General Chiwenga, or someone else? Will President Mnangagwa retire peacefully? (Part 2) – Nehanda Radio
item.description: In this second and final part of the article, I continue to examine the potential outcomes of ZANU-PF’s succession politics, focusing on whether Kudakwashe Tagwirei (whom I metaphorically refer to as “Mamvura”) will succeed in his presumed bid for the presidency, whether General Constantino Chiwenga will recover his political standing and take over, whether someone else will ascend to the throne, and whether President Mnangagwa will ultimately retire in peace.

item.title: The uneasy peace: Grace Mugabe, Mnangagwa and the politics of controlled memory – Nehanda Radio
item.description: At a recent public function, the opening of The Sprout Restaurant in Harare, we saw former First Lady Grace Mugabe moving within the same orbit as senior ZANU PF figures, her presence neither resisted nor theatrically embraced.

item.title: Zimbabwe police crack down on officers posting content in uniform – Nehanda Radio
item.description: Zimbabwe’s police force has issued a nationwide directive ordering officers to remove all social media content showing themselves in uniform

item.title: “Police know drug suppliers”: Malloti points to Mbare Zanu-PF councillor ‘Dhama’ – Nehanda Radio
item.description: Simbarashe Chanachimwe, better known as Dhama, an alleged Mbare drug dealer arrested in 2023 and now serving as a councillor, has been named in fresh allegations by Zimdancehall artist Malloti Rose, who claims that authorities are turning a blind eye not only to him but also to other influential figures allegedly controlling Harare’s drug trade.

item.title: Zanu PF re-tests the ground for a referendum on Constitutional Amendment No. 3 – Nehanda Radio
item.description: The ruling ZANU-PF party says there will be no referendum on Constitutional Amendment Bill No. 3, come hell or thunder. Yet its political actions increasingly resemble a party preparing for one.

item.title: Open letter to Rt Air Marshall Henry Muchena – Nehanda Radio
item.description: As a young citizen of this country, I write in response not only to a well-earned rebuttal towards Sabhuku T. Mliswa, written under your name, but generally, to many other issues you've dutifully raised since the introduction of CAB3.

item.title: $25m divorce bombshell rocks Chivayo as ex-wife seeks US$40k a month – Nehanda Radio
item.description: A high-stakes divorce battle involving controversial businessman Wicknell Chivayo has erupted into the open, with his former partner tabling eye-watering financial demands — including a $25 million payout, hefty monthly maintenance, and a garage of ultra-luxury cars.
